hypothesis: The released contrastive StyleDistance encoder may provide more transferable LLM style information than LUAR; this is a separately recorded representation change after v5 and v6 failed their gates.
representation: Preserve raw text and case. Tokenize once without truncation; consecutive nonoverlapping windows of up to 510 content tokens plus two RoBERTa specials. Apply released attention-mask token-mean pooling in each window, aggregate windows weighted by non-padding token count including specials, then L2-normalize once per passage. Dynamic token padding within at most eight-window batches. No custom remote code. Long-text aggregation is an explicit project extension of the released single-window pooling. Never aggregate distinct rows.
pooling: Normalize log probabilities from the fixed StyleDistance logistic probe per row. Blend with separately normalized completed v4 evidence as defined in v5; no LUAR or v6 classifier output is used.
selection: Highest original-fold balanced accuracy among exactly two recipes; ties favor standalone. Evaluate only the winner on robustness folds. No threshold changes or parameter/weight search after scores.
limitations: Both validation partitions reuse labeled data and previously inspected splits; neither is an untouched holdout.
Selecting between two recipes introduces selection optimism; group-bootstrap intervals are descriptive only.
The cited paper does not establish transfer to this 18-class competition or guarantee any leaderboard gain.
No blind submission if the frozen gates fail. A later distinct experiment requires a separately recorded plan.
